findings.problem: BatchWorkflow uses status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> instead of an enum/typestate state machine, allowing illegal states such as status="pending" with is_sent=true, or both booleans false while a timestamp exists.
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct or mutate BatchWorkflow into any combination of status/flags, making state transitions unenforceable and business logic dependent on fragile boolean checks
findings.fix: Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single BatchStatus enum (e.g., Pending, Validated, Sent { at: sent_at_ms }) so invalid state combinations are unrepresentable

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option) enter the domain struct without a parse boundary or smart constructor; all fields are pub.
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct BatchWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "banana".into(), is_validated: true, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None } directly, bypassing all domain invariants
findings.fix: Make fields private, remove pub visibility, and provide a fallible constructor or factory that validates id is non-empty, status is a known variant, and is_sent implies a non-null timestamp

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() to set status, which allocates a heap String each call and encodes state as a literal string instead of an enum variant.
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition; string literals are typos-prone and not exhaustively checkable by the compiler
findings.fix: Replace status String with an enum; mark_sent should construct the appropriate enum variant (e.g., BatchStatus::Sent { at: now() }) without heap allocation for the state itself

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of BatchWorkflow and mutates it freely without enforcing preconditions (e.g., must be validated before sending, id must be non-empty).
findings.failure_mode: any BatchWorkflow can be marked sent regardless of validation state, violating business invariants that should be enforced at the type level
findings.fix: Use a typestate pattern: separate ValidatedBatchWorkflow and SentBatchWorkflow types, or an enum with a Sent variant requiring explicit construction only after validation

findings.problem: mark_sent embeds domain logic (status mutation, flag toggling) directly in a free function operating on a struct with mutable public fields, instead of encapsulating behavior in a module with invariants.
findings.failure_mode: no module-level enforcement of invariants; any caller can bypass mark_sent and mutate fields directly since they are pub
findings.fix: Encapsulate BatchWorkflow in a module, make all fields private, and expose only safe transition methods or reconstructive functions that return the next typestate

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics; sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a raw epoch without a timestamp newtype.
findings.failure_mode: any string can be used as an id (no length/format validation); raw u64 epoch ms can be confused with seconds, nanoseconds, or other units
findings.fix: Introduce BatchId(newtype over String or u64) and TimestampMs(newtype over u64) with domain-specific constructors and display formatting

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any throughput/latency claim
no profiler or allocation evidence for the .to_string() hot path
no command evidence (cargo test, cargo fmt, cargo clippy) was run
no second-ring evidence such as Miri, Kani, or property tests
residual_risk: static review only; no commands run. The crate is a minimal two-item module with no tests, no benchmarks, and no proof artifacts. All findings are based on structural and semantic inspection against Holzman Rust doctrine. The typestate and parse-boundary violations are the highest risk: illegal states are fully representable and constructable.
